cds.title: University of Denver Common Data Set 2025-2026 (PDF, Institutional Research; page headers read 2024-2025 but the data are Fall 2025)

cost.notes: From the CDS G1 and G5 (which ask for 2026-27 costs and list these amounts, although the box 'costs not available' is ticked) and the University of Denver international tuition page, which states the same figures for 2026-2027 (three quarters, fall/winter/spring): tuition $63,720 ($21,240 per quarter; $1,770 per credit hour), student fees $1,584, on-campus housing $11,283 plus meals $7,532 (food and housing $18,815), books and supplies $1,000. The international page also lists health insurance $3,998 (the DU student plan, waivable with comparable coverage), personal expenses $1,782 and transportation $627, and publishes a total estimated cost of $91,526 that includes them; other_usd is left empty so the published total is not rebuilt from parts.

stats.notes: From the Common Data Set (Fall 2025 entering class; the PDF's page headers say 2024-2025 but the questions and data are for Fall 2025): 16,637 applied, 14,205 admitted, 1,174 enrolled. Residency rows (in-state / out-of-state / international) add up to the totals. International (by address) first-years: 981 applied, 616 admitted, 42 enrolled; the B2 nonresident-alien first-year count is 35. Early decision figures cover the binding ED rounds only (the CDS also lists a non-binding early action plan but gives no EA counts). The waiting list is tiny (22 offered, 4 accepted, none admitted). SAT/ACT submission is optional: 25% of enrolled first-years submitted the SAT (295) and 11% the ACT (130); the percentile ranges cover those submitters only. The GPA breakdown is the 'all enrolled students' column (high-school GPA, 99.4% reported); percentages add to 100.1% because of rounding. Undergraduate enrollment (5,766) and the nonresident count (170) are the B1/B2 'Total Undergraduates' figures. Admit rate by these counts is about 85%.

cds_test_policy.notes: From CDS C8: SAT or ACT 'not required for admission, but considered if submitted'. DU has been test-optional since 2019.
